source.title: Reverse Replay of Hippocampal Place Cells Is Uniquely Modulated by Changing Reward.

confidence_rationale: Directly extends the Foster & Wilson 2006 reverse-replay finding already tagged to ARC-028 (targeted_review_connectome_arc_028) toward MECH-290's specific credit-assignment framing: this paper shows reverse (but not forward) replay rate scales with reward MAGNITUDE CHANGES at the reward location, which is evidence that reverse replay is a reward/credit-carrying signal rather than mere structural memory consolidation. This is the strongest single biological anchor available for 'reverse replay functions as reward-linked credit propagation,' the premise MECH-290 imports into REE as a backward TD-style sweep. Confidence held at 0.55 because the paper's DV is REPLAY RATE / EVENT FREQUENCY at the reward site, not a per-step, discount-weighted retroactive VALUE UPDATE along the preceding trajectory -- MECH-290's specific claim (discount^(T-t) weighted propagation through preceding states) is a further inferential step the paper's own data do not directly test.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats performing a spatial alternation task with a manipulated reward magnitude, reverse-ordered hippocampal place-cell replay events (but not forward-ordered ones) increased in rate when reward was increased and decreased in rate when reward was decreased, at the reward location itself. Forward replay showed no such reward-dependent modulation. The authors conclude this demonstrates 'a unique relationship between reverse replay and reward processing' distinct from any general memory-consolidation role.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-290 imports the reverse-replay phenomenon as the biological grounding for HippocampalModule's backward_credit_sweep(): a discount-weighted propagation of the terminal outcome (goal contact / failure) backward through the just-executed trajectory's buffered states. This paper strengthens that grounding specifically on the REWARD-LINKAGE half of the claim (reverse replay is not just structural replay, it tracks reward), which is the load-bearing premise for treating reverse replay as a credit-assignment signal rather than a memory-rehearsal signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's dependent variable is the RATE of reverse-replay EVENTS as a function of reward magnitude change, not a per-step, discount-weighted UPDATE of value estimates at each preceding state as MECH-290's discount^(T-t) formula specifies. It is evidence that reverse replay carries reward information at all, which is necessary but not sufficient for the specific TD-style backward-sweep mechanism MECH-290 claims; it does not itself demonstrate step-wise discounted credit propagation.
mapping.source_context: Freely-moving rats on a W-track spatial alternation task with experimenter-manipulated reward magnitude (increased/decreased water reward) at fixed reward wells; place-cell tetrode recordings during sharp-wave ripples in the awake state.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Neuron, well-cited, direct single-unit electrophysiology from the same lab as the foundational Foster & Wilson 2006 finding already grounding ARC-028). Mapping fidelity moderate: strengthens the reward-linkage premise but does not directly test the discount-weighted per-step propagation MECH-290 specifically claims.
